answer: Clock-skew fingerprinting resists sybils cheaply. Every machine's quartz crystal oscillator drifts at a device-unique rate; a rotating jury times each identity's signed heartbeats and reads that drift as a hardware signal no software can forge. Clones packed on one box share one crystal, so their signatures collapse into a single cluster, get flagged, and every bond behind them is slashed. A healthy network looks like an orchard of distinct trees: faking N identities needs N separate physical oscillators, paying linear N-times real hardware and power, never amortized.
